observations.observation: JunoCam and JIRAM tracked the central north polar cyclone and eight surrounding cyclones over multiple orbits; their motion is consistent with poleward beta drift, mutual interaction, oscillation around central positions, and slow westward drift.
NASA reported 26 Juno radio-occultation soundings; the north polar stratospheric cap was about 11 degC cooler than its surroundings and was encircled by winds exceeding 161 km/h.
JIRAM maps Jupiter thermal emission near 4.8 micrometres and auroral emission near 3.45 micrometres.
Juno MWR measurements show that at least two polar storms extend at least 100 km below Jupiter cloud tops.
Juno detected shallow lightning at high altitude; NASA interprets it as electrical discharge in ammonia-water clouds formed when lofted water ice encounters ammonia.
At extreme pressure deep inside Jupiter, hydrogen becomes electrically conducting liquid metallic hydrogen; this region is a leading explanation for Jupiter strong magnetic dynamo.
Jupiter has exceptionally bright auroras produced as charged particles precipitate into the atmosphere; Juno observes the particles, fields, and auroral emissions.
